messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert triggered -> HIGH: nccl-kernel-oops on pg=gpupool-7 (priority: P1)
incident-bot: summary: multi-GPU collective hang + kernel oops -> containerd restarted on node gpu-7b; multiple TP ranks stuck in rendezvous; automated retries failing

maya: seeing repeated kernel oops logs on gpu-7b, kernel message: 'kernel: [12345.678901] NMI: CPU: ... Oops: kernel paging request'
maya: tp rank 0..7 report hang in allreduce, ranks 2 and 3 show 'ncclPeerTimeout'

jordan: @maya can you paste recent journalctl / dmesg snippet? any Xid mentions (Xid 79 / 13)?
maya: pasted below:
```
Mar 15 03:20:11 gpu-7b kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:17:00): 79, pid=31415, GPU has fallen off the bus.
Mar 15 03:20:11 gpu-7b kernel: oom-kill: task python3:31415 score 987 or sacrifice child
Mar 15 03:20:12 gpu-7b containerd[1234]: container "rundir-tp-shard-3" terminated: exit_code=137
Mar 15 03:20:12 gpu-7b nccl: NCCL WARN Call to allReduce timed out after 120s
```

samir: looks like kernel/Xid -> driver crash -> container restart -> nccl communicator lost state -> rendezvous failure cascade

liz: customer-impact: dedicated customer 'ml-analytics' reported 503s between 03:20-03:26; other hosted jobs saw tail latency spike ~3x

devin: oncall: @eng-runtime-oncall can you take lead? we'll need kernel oops triage + mitigation to restore shards without data loss

eng-runtime-oncall: taking it. quick plan: 1) drain gpupool-7 from scheduling, 2) mark node offline in scheduler, 3) spawn TP replica on warm spare, 4) attempt safe restart path for remaining containers, 5) collect full kernel oops and GPU panic logs

maya: draining now: `kubectl cordon gpu-7b` and scaling down non-critical pods on pool

ops-bot: Node gpu-7b cordoned by maya at 2491234089

jordan: while we drain, set NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1 on new shards and add NCCL_DEBUG=INFO for 24h for extra visibility

samir: also recommend `export NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=NET` to avoid buggy P2P paths during driver issues (temporary)

eng-runtime-oncall: starting canary reschedule to gpupool-9 (single-shard hot-standby). will route 10% traffic for 5m then scale if stable

maya: I'm grabbing `dmesg -T` and full `journalctl -k -u gpu-manager --since \"1 hour ago\"` to attach to incident ticket

liz: I've opened INC-2026-314 with customer impact notes and emailed primary contact; noting we have partial degradation, some 503s and retries. ETA update at 03:45UTC

jordan: found additional hint in /var/log/nvidia-installer.log: driver re-init triggered around kernel oops; suspect kernel+driver mismatch after live driver update window earlier today
devin: any chance automatic driver update happened? patch window was scheduled but flagged no-cb; need to confirm 

maya: no scheduled driver push for gpupool-7 this week in ops calendar, looks manual/rare; collecting apt/dpkg logs now

eng-runtime-oncall: mitigation steps in flight: 
- drained node and stopped new allocations
- restarted nccl communicator cleanup on surviving ranks via graceful SIGUSR1 to python loop (to trigger reinit)
- initiated canary on gpupool-9 with NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1 and NCCL_DEBUG=INFO

samir: note: SIGUSR1 is our configured graceful-reconnect trigger; if process not responsive, we `kill -9` followed by restart to ensure kernel state cleared

ops-bot: Canary on gpupool-9 reported healthy for 6m, latency within baseline

jordan: rolling traffic: moving 40% now. watch for reconnect errors in logs (nccl comm create / rendezvous)

maya: we still see one remaining pod stuck in CrashLoopBackOff on gpu-7b: `rundir-tp-shard-3`, logs show memory map corruption prior to oom kill

eng-runtime-oncall: we will perform node reboot for gpupool-7 after collecting crash artifacts; reboot will clear GPU driver state. scheduling now - ETA 10m

liz: customer update drafted: \"We experienced a GPU driver/kernel error that caused a subset of multi-GPU workloads to fail. We're mitigating by draining affected nodes and rescheduling to healthy capacity; a reboot is scheduled. We'll follow up with root cause.\" Send at 03:35UTC?
jordan: send now, include that no persistent data lost, and that a small set of requests may have seen 5xxs and retries

maya: attaching small dump from container before it died:
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File \"/app/run.py\", line 242, in <module>
    outputs = model.parallel_allreduce(tensors)
  File \"/usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/nccl_bindings.py\", line 88, in allreduce
    raise NCCLException('Call timed out')
NCCLException: Call timed out after 120s
```

samir: after reboot we'll validate PCIe topology `nvidia-smi topo -m` and run `nv_peer_mem` tests, then mark node healthy only after two successful tensor-parallel test jobs

eng-runtime-oncall: gpupool-7 reboot started at 2491234320

ops-bot: Node gpu-7b reboot completed at 2491234360; kubelet rejoined cluster, but node ready state took ~80s

jordan: post-reboot checks: `nvidia-smi` shows all GPUs present, no ECC errors, driver 525.85 loaded, but we see one GPU with high ECC counts earlier (now zero counters after reset). running nccl unit-test suite on node (allreduce/allgather for TP shapes)

maya: nccl unit-tests passed for allreduce shapes 1..8 on node after reboot. re-enabling scheduling to gpupool-7 but keep initial weight low for 15m

eng-runtime-oncall: promoted canary and now back-filling shards to original capacity; monitoring for 30m window. will keep NCCL_DEBUG enabled until 24h after finish

liz: customer notified of resolution and that we're doing follow-up RCA; tagging affected accounts and creating postmortem ticket PM-2026-029

devin: action items assigned: 
- eng-runtime: deep RCA for kernel oops root cause (possible driver/firmware mismatch) (owner: eng-runtime-oncall)
- infra: confirm no automatic driver pushes (owner: jordan)
- sres: add proactive node health checks for ECC/driver anomalies (owner: samir)
- product ops: update customer comms template for GPU cascade incidents (owner: liz)

eng-runtime-oncall: note: temporary mitigations we applied that may become runbook updates: 
- enable NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING by default on Dedicated for canary rollouts
- include SIGUSR1 graceful-reconnect in our container entrypoint docs
- add preemptive driver/firmware parity check to node's preflight before scheduling TP workloads

jordan: closing pager on this thread once 30m stable window completes; leave thread open for RCA attachments

maya: thanks all, handing off final logs to PM ticket.

eng-runtime-oncall: last check-in at 2491234499: cluster stable, no further 5xxs; marking incident as mitigated, will compile RCA notes for postmortem.
